name: query-builder

frames.best_why: The field dropdown is open over a full set of rule rows, showing both the structure and the picker.

tagline: Stack rows of field, operator and value to build an AND/OR filter.
summary: A visual filter composer where each row picks a field, an operator and a value, joined by And or Or. Add rule grows the list, Add group nests an indented subgroup, and each row can be removed.
appearance: A dark form on black: a small Where label followed by rows of rounded outlined dropdowns and an input, each row ending in a bin icon, with a thin And selector at the left of later rows. Below the rows sit quiet Add rule and Add group links.
behaviour: Choosing a field swaps the operator list and the value control to match it, so a date field gets a date picker and Status gets a short list. Add rule appends a row and Add group nests an indented subgroup; the small And or Or select changes how rows combine.
demo_content: Rules for Status is Todo, Estimate is at least 5 and Title contains checkout, on a task tracker.
search_phrases: visual filter rules with and or
build a search with nested conditions
add rows of field operator value
filter panel for a data table
where clause editor for non coders
how to let users combine several filters
use_when: Users must combine several filters with AND/OR logic and see the rule structure while building it.
avoid_when: It is a set of parts needing a fields schema and controlled query state, not a drop-in search box.
customise: Pass a fields schema and a controlled query value, then arrange the rows from the exported parts; labels, maxDepth and disabled are props. The order and layout of the controls are yours.
weight_why: A handful of dropdowns and popovers with nothing animating at rest.

a11y.note: Fields, operators and values carry labels and the rules expose list roles; no reduced-motion check exists, though little moves.

issues: The dim grey selects and hairline borders on black make the rule structure hard to scan.
The demo shows no resulting query or run button, so it is unclear what the built filter is for.
polish_why: Tidy, consistent control rows with a clear nesting model; dim text is hard to scan.
